review.tagline: Train a 64M-parameter LLM from scratch in plain PyTorch
review.summary: MiniMind is a from-scratch implementation of a small Qwen3-style decoder-only LLM (64M dense, 198M-A64M MoE) with each training stage written in native PyTorch: pretrain, SFT, LoRA, DPO, PPO/GRPO/CISPO, agentic RL and distillation. It ships datasets, a 6,400-token tokenizer, an OpenAI-compatible server and a Streamlit chat UI. The README states one SFT epoch takes about 2 hours on a single 3090.
review.audience: Engineers learning LLM internals by pretraining and fine-tuning small models
strengths: Core algorithms (LoRA, DPO, PPO/GRPO) written in plain PyTorch, not wrapped from trl or peft
Open datasets for each stage, with mini variants (1.2GB pretrain, 1.6GB SFT) for quick runs
Weights convert to transformers, llama.cpp, vllm and ollama; ollama and vllm usage is documented
Checkpoint resume, DDP and DeepSpeed multi-GPU, wandb or swanlab logging
weaknesses: Models are tiny (64M), so output quality is far below mainstream LLMs
README is primarily in Chinese; the English version is a separate file
Training data is largely synthetic and distilled, with mixed source licenses
Native MoE training is about 50% slower than dense, per the README
needs: Needs PyTorch, transformers, streamlit (optional WebUI), swanlab or wandb (optional)
Models: minimind-3 (64M), minimind-3-moe (198M-A64M), minimind2 series, Transformers format, llama.cpp
